actionable_failures.title: Final corrected contract still requires unsourced blue dominance
actionable_failures.finding: Final candidate-plan.v2.json retains 'The dominant colour treatment...' under requirement authority. BRIEF.md:3 requires use of the UI cool blue accent and says a fixed palette is not required; it does not require the accent to dominate the composition. The caller checks hue/hex/palette flexibility but never compares the dominant qualifier, then adopts the unchanged contract as consistent.
actionable_failures.counterexample: A mostly neutral asymmetrical completion check or backing shape with a clearly visible cool-blue edge/inset can satisfy the brief, yet fail a literal dominant-blue treatment rule. Merely allowing other blue hues or multiple tones does not test this alternative.
actionable_failures.impact: Prospective required criteria can reject source-conforming art; the claimed independent semantic consistency and completed correction are not established. This does not invalidate the actual all-blue fixture, historical verdict identity, source-consumer mapping or exact continuation.
actionable_failures.action: Preserve this attempt and final artifacts. In a new proposal, retain the required visible accent outcome and either remove dominant composition from required criteria or separate it as an explicit scoped expert sample choice. Independently compare every qualifying clause against original wording and a counterexample before adopting. Do not transplant historical verdicts or create a provider job for this correction.

minor_observations.title: Bounding-box center wording doubles the offset
minor_observations.finding: specialist-assessment says the bbox is one pixel right/down from the geometric cell center, while its own exclusive bbox [3,4,14,13] yields center (8.5,8.5) versus cell center (8,8): a half-pixel offset on each axis. The margin imbalance is one pixel.
minor_observations.action: If carrying this diagnostic forward, call it a half-pixel bbox-center offset or one-pixel margin imbalance. No rejection rule or historical acceptance change follows.
minor_observations.severity_boundary: Informational numerical precision issue; not a second substantive authority failure.
